sonnet.problem: The story card asks 'So how do they change direction?', which assumes the creatures change direction. The text says they did not turn and each one went straight ahead (1:9, 1:12). The card then leads into a card asking whether they turn.
sonnet.rule: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

sonnet.problem: The joke about having one gold base and still tipping into the flour doesn't match the wheel-within-a-wheel detail. The wheels are about how they look and how they go in any direction, not about tipping over, so a stranger would say 'huh?'.
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

sonnet.problem: The same punchline shape repeats across the lesson: a grand detail from the vision, then a small self-deprecating 'I can't even do X' kitchen line. It shows up in stop 1 cards 5, 11 and 13 and stop 2 cards 3, 8 and 9. Three of them are oven jokes (oven light, oven dial, oven window).
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.
